chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Fadl ibn Ghazwan, from al-Hakam ibn al-Hukaym, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I go to the market and need to urinate, and there is no water with me. Then I wipe it and dry it with my hand, then I wipe my hand on the wall and the ground, then I scratch my body after that.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.'
ai.seo_question: How to purify urine stains without water?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the principle of *al-istishab* (presumption of continuity) and the flexibility of *al-tayyub* (drying) in Shia jurisprudence when water is scarce. It highlights the practical leniency granted by Imam al-Sadiq (AS), validating that mechanical removal of impurity via hand-wiping and surface-drying suffices for ritual purity without the need for extensive washing.
